projects.title: ChessBD
projects.tagline: A chess platform for the Bangladesh chess community.
projects.description: Game analysis with Stockfish 17, player profiles and leaderboards, events, clubs, a forum, news and interactive lessons, in one place for Bangladeshi players.
projects.overview:
ChessBD brings the tools a chess community needs into one site for players in Bangladesh.

### Analysis

- **Game review** of any PGN with the Stockfish 17 engine: every move is classified (brilliant, great, best, excellent, good, inaccuracy, mistake, miss, blunder), with win percentages, an evaluation graph and best-move suggestions.
- **An engine board** for exploring positions, **bots** at several strengths, and **puzzles** for tactics training.

### Community

- **Player profiles** with statistics, ratings and game history, and **leaderboards**.
- **Events** for tournaments, a **club directory**, a **forum** and a **news** feed.

### Learning

- Step-by-step **interactive lessons** and **video tutorials**.

### Stack

A React and Vite front end, with Firebase and Supabase behind it and chess.js for move handling.

projects.overview:
The Institute for Theoretical and Computational Physics Research (ITCPR) aims to provide research opportunities to people typically overlooked in science. I co-founded the institute and serve as its Director of Operations. Its work happens across a set of web apps I built, all behind one sign-on.

### One login, many apps

The **SSO** service issues the session every other app trusts, so members sign in once and move between the portal, CodeLab, the terminal and the forum.

### For research

- The **Portal** is the workspace: groups, projects, courses, meetings and guides.
- **CodeLab** is where members share code.
- The **Terminal** is a browser-based terminal with command history, a nano-style editor and MuMax3 simulation jobs, with a notification when a job finishes.

### For the community

- A **Forum** with voting, comments, search and Markdown with LaTeX.
- **Events** for schools, seminars and workshops, a **Library**, a **physics news** feed and interactive **physics engines**.

### Stack

Each app is a React and Vite front end on Firebase and Supabase, sharing the same authentication.

projects.title: GitLaTeX
projects.tagline: A local, Git-native LaTeX editor that runs in your browser.
projects.description: Write in a Monaco editor, compile to PDF and push to GitHub, without Overleaf, a subscription or your files leaving your machine. Published on PyPI.
projects.overview:
GitLaTeX is a local, Git-native LaTeX editor that runs in the browser: write in a Monaco editor, compile to PDF, and push to GitHub, without Overleaf, a subscription, or your files ever leaving your own machine. Your `.tex` files are plain files on disk, and your history is plain Git.

```bash
pip install gitlatex
gitlatex
```

It opens at `http://localhost:5000`. Clone a repository or create a folder, and start writing; changes save as you type.

### Why build it

Overleaf is excellent until you want your files on your own disk, your own Git remote, and no upload limits. GitLaTeX keeps the same shape of workflow (editor, live PDF, one-click compile) but runs everything locally against a real repository, so unpublished work never leaves your machine.

### Editor

- Built on **Monaco**, the editor behind VS Code, with LaTeX and BibTeX highlighting in light and dark themes.
- **Autocomplete** for 150+ commands and 50+ environments. Inside `\ref{}` and `\cite{}` it completes from the project's own labels and `.bib` keys, showing each entry's title, author and year.
- A **document outline** that follows the cursor, and matched `\begin`/`\end` colouring so an unclosed environment is obvious.

### LaTeX-aware spell checking

- Skips comments, math, verbatim blocks and the arguments of `\ref`, `\cite`, `\url` and friends, so only prose is checked.
- Built for papers: coinages like *nanowire* or *anti-symmetric* resolve against their parts instead of being flagged, with a personal dictionary that persists across projects.

### Compiling

- **One click to PDF**, shown beside the editor, with `pdflatex`, `xelatex` or `lualatex`.
- **Full multi-pass builds**: `biber` or `bibtex` runs when needed and the engine reruns until references settle, so no more compiling three times to clear `??`.
- Errors and warnings are parsed from the log into a **clickable problems list** that jumps to the line.
- An optional **remote compiler API** lets it build on a web service, so no TeX distribution is needed locally.

### Git

- Status, diff, pull and push from the toolbar; push stages, commits and pushes in one action.
- A **version history** panel with per-file changes, and side-by-side diffs between any two commits.

### Collaboration

An optional relay ([gitlatex-collab](https://github.com/abdussamiakanda/gitlatex-collab)) on Cloudflare Workers lets a few co-authors edit the same project in real time. It only relays text: each collaborator still saves, compiles and commits on their own machine.

### How it's built

A **Flask** server with a strict split: `services/` holds the logic (LaTeX runs and log parsing, spell checking on symspellpy, Git through GitPython, the project index for autocomplete) and knows nothing about HTTP, while `routes/` holds thin blueprints in front of it.

Built and maintained with [Md Atiqur Rahman](https://github.com/revolutionibus). Released under the ISC license.

projects.title: FloorLab
projects.tagline: A floor plan designer with a 3D view.
projects.description: Draw 2D floor plans with walls, doors, windows and rooms, adjust colours and dimensions, walk around them in 3D, save to the cloud and export to JSON or PNG.
projects.overview:
FloorLab is a floor plan designer in the browser.

### What it does

- Draw **2D floor plans** with walls, doors, windows and rooms.
- Customise **colours and dimensions**.
- View the plan in **3D**.
- **Save to the cloud** under your Google account, and **export** to JSON or PNG.

### Stack

- **React 19** and **Vite 7**, with React Router protecting signed-in routes.
- **Three.js** through **React Three Fiber** and **drei** for the 3D viewer.
- **Firebase**: Google sign-in and Firestore, with security rules scoped to each user's plans.
